matches.definition: To have a particular identity, quality, or condition.
To be in a particular place, or to exist.
To apply force to something to move it toward yourself or in a particular direction.
To go in a certain direction or head toward a place.
To suffer, endure, or go through difficulties.
matches.glosses: to go through, to suffer, to endure

matches.definition: To push yourself off the ground into the air or over an obstacle using your legs.
matches.glosses: to jump, to leap, to hop

matches.definition: To move something so that an opening is covered, or to stop being open for business.
To stop the operation of a light, machine, or electrical device, or to end a phone call.
matches.glosses: to turn off, to switch off, to hang up

matches.definition: To reserve or arrange a ticket, room, table, or appointment in advance.
To make it easier for someone to do something by offering aid or doing part of the work.
To take part in a game, sport, or recreational activity.
To perform music on a musical instrument.
To take hold of something with the hands.
To intercept and hold something moving, or to capture someone or something.
To take up or occupy a seat, space, or place.
To arrange for a message, letter, or object to go or be taken to someone.
To tell or arrange for a person to go to a particular place.
To go up using hands and feet, especially on a steep surface.
To come first in a game or competition, or to defeat an opponent.
To receive money for working, or to gain something useful.
To go to see a person or a place for a short time.
To no longer have something, or not know where it is.
To not win a game, competition, or match.
To arrive too late for a bus, train, flight, or event.
To be in an upright position on your feet, or to remain upright.
To be alive; to lead a particular kind of life.
To have your home in a place.
To move through water by using your arms and legs.
To start doing something, or (of an event or period) to start happening.
To have a need for something or someone.
To fail to remember a fact, a person, or to do something.
To speak to or contact someone by telephone.
To perceive or notice someone or something with your eyes.
To look at something for a period of time, such as a film, television program, or match.
To meet or visit someone by arrangement.
To move quickly on foot, faster than walking.
To move or act hurriedly; to rush around.
To flow, of water or another liquid, or of a tap.
To do work or have a job.
To operate or function properly, like a machine or device.
To control the movement of a car or other vehicle.
To take someone to a place, or (of a road or path) to go to a place.
To be familiar with a person or place, or (especially in the past tense) to meet someone for the first time.
To have information about something; to be aware of a fact (more formal than ξέρω).
To use one's voice to produce words or have a conversation.
To be able to communicate in a particular language.
To move toward the speaker or toward a particular place; to arrive.
Of a time or event: to approach or be about to happen.
To place something in a particular position or add something (such as an ingredient or liquid).
To dress oneself in a piece of clothing or an accessory.
To start a machine, appliance, or music playing.
To stay in a place or delay action until someone arrives or something happens.
To regard something as likely to happen, or to anticipate an arrival.
To move down from a higher position, or to lose one's balance and hit the ground.
To decrease in amount, value, or intensity.
To decide which one you want from a group of things or people.
To put a question to someone in order to get information.
To form letters, words, or texts on paper or a screen.
To register someone (or in the passive 'γράφομαι', oneself) for a school, club, or course.
To capture sound, video, or data on a device or disc.
To use your mind to consider something, reflect on someone or something, or hold an opinion.
To have a plan or intention to do something.
To construct a building, wall, or other physical structure.
To develop or establish something non-physical, such as a relationship, trust, or a career, over time.
To wish to have or do something.
To require something for a purpose, or to take a certain amount of time or effort.
To express something in words, or to give information to someone.
To suggest an idea or ask someone's opinion about a plan.
To intend to convey a particular meaning (especially in 'τι θα πει' = what does it mean).
To carry or move something or someone from one place to another, especially when it is heavy or takes effort.
To stop sleeping and become awake.
To cause someone to stop sleeping.
To get to a place, especially at the end of a journey.
To be as much or as many as needed.
To impart knowledge or skill to someone, especially in a school or university.
To be in or move into a seated position.
To remain in a place or spend time somewhere.
To go from one place to another, especially over a long distance or to another country.
To separate or cause something hard to separate into pieces, or to crack and stop working.
To have information or facts in your mind, or to be familiar with a person or place.
To have the skill or ability to do something (followed by να or a noun).
To move or travel through the air (of a bird, aircraft, or passenger).
To send something through the air with your hand, or to get rid of something as rubbish.
To move forward on foot at a normal speed.
To make a picture using pencils, pens, or paint.
To rest with your eyes closed in a natural state of unconsciousness, or to fall into this state.
To come to a halt or to bring an ongoing action to an end.
To perceive a sound with the ears.
To pay attention to a sound or to someone speaking.
To receive news or information about something.
To acquire knowledge or a skill through study, practice, or experience.
To hear or discover news or information about something.
To look at written words and understand what they mean.
To spend time learning and preparing for a class or exam.
To make musical sounds with the voice.
To clean something with water and usually soap.
To go away from a place or person.
To move one's body rhythmically to music.
To apply physical force to something or someone in order to move them away.
To move something like a door, window, or container so it is no longer shut, or of a business, to begin operating for the day.
To start the flow of electricity or water in a light, tap, or appliance.
To grasp the meaning of words, information, or a language.
To become aware of a fact or situation.
To speak or write back to someone who has asked a question or written to you.
To react to an action, situation, or challenge.
To move or travel from one place to another.
To proceed or turn out in a particular way.
To repair something that is broken or not working properly.
To remove mistakes from something written or spoken, or to put right a fault.
To remove dirt, stains, or mess from a place or object.
To remove the skin, shell, or inedible parts from food before eating or cooking.
To carry or take someone or something to the place where the speaker or listener is.
To cause a state or result, or to bring in money.
To touch someone or something with your lips as a sign of love, affection, or greeting.
To divide, slice, or trim something using a sharp tool such as a knife or scissors.
To give up a habit, or to cut off a supply or connection.
To buy or issue a ticket, receipt, or fine.
To pick up, grasp, or take something or someone with you.
To buy or receive something.
To use a means of public transport.
To come together with someone, either by arrangement or by chance.
To come across or face something such as a difficulty or obstacle.
To discover or locate something or someone, either after searching or by chance.
To have a particular opinion or impression of someone or something.
To direct your eyes toward someone or something.
To examine or check something to get information or see its condition.
To hand something over to someone else or transfer possession.
To provide or offer something such as a result, opportunity, or payment.
matches.glosses: to give, to offer, to provide

matches.definition: To hold someone close in your arms to show love or affection.
To accept or support an idea, cause, or group enthusiastically.
To complete an activity, or (of an event or period) to come to an end.
matches.glosses: to finish, to complete, to end

matches.definition: Of a supply or item: to be completely used up so that none is left.
matches.glosses: to run out, to be all gone

matches.definition: To keep a person, fact, or event in your mind, or to bring it back into your thoughts.
To own, hold, or possess something, or to be connected with someone or something.
To experience a physical feeling, illness, or state of mind.
To capture an image or video with a camera or phone.
To perform as an actor in a play, film, or television show.
To stop moving or pause briefly, or to dwell on a topic.
To accidentally leave something behind in a place.
To present two people to each other so they can make acquaintance.
To lie down in bed, especially in order to sleep.
To use a particular name for someone or something.
To accompany someone or carry something to a place.
To telephone someone (often with τηλέφωνο).
To take care of someone or attend to a matter.
matches.glosses: look after, take care of, mind

matches.definition: To sit or take an examination, or to give a performance.
matches.glosses: to take, to sit, to give

matches.definition: Used as an auxiliary verb with the non-finite verb form to make perfect tenses.
